To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gelation and shears stability of blends of the conjugated polymer P3HT with the non fullerene small molecule acceptor o IDTRB is a function of the P3HTo IDTBR concentrations and the solvent used.

the gelation dynamics of P3 HT and P3 HT/PC60BM and oIDTBR blends under sub ambient conditions are functions of the P 3 HT and oIDT BR concentrations, the solvent and the shearing history, and that the gel strengths of P3 HT gels and blends of P 3 HT/PC 60 BM and oIDT RB under sub ambient conditions decrease with increasing shear rates.

the rheological material functions of the gels of P 3HT and blends with small molecule acceptor o IDTRB formed upon quench to sub zero temperatures are functions of P 3 HT and acceptor concentration, the solvent used, and the shearing history.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the sub ambient shearing and gelation of P 3 HT solutions and blends towards active layer fabrication in bulk heterojunc tion organic solar cells.
the rheology of polymer blends used as active layers in bulk heterojucton organic solar cells.
the dynamics of the gel formation of P3HT blends and their shearing under sub ambient conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gelation dynamics of P3HTo IDTBR solutions are not only dependent on the P3HT concentration but also on the shearing conditions, and that the resulting gel strengths are not sufficient to allow processing of the gels via steady shear flows.

the processing of P3HT gelled solutions with small molecule acceptor under sub ambient conditions is possible, but the resulting active layers are not stable under shear, thus limiting the potential of this processing route to fabricate OSC active layers.
the gelation behavior and the shearing history of the P3HTo IDTBR gels are functions of the PTHTo IDTBR concentration, solvent and the shearing condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gelation and subsequent shearing dynamics of P3Ht with o IDTBR can provide a new processing route for the formation of the active layers in bulk heterojuncton solar cells.
the rheology of the P3HP gels formed at sub zero temperatures can be used to understand and control the processing conditions of the active layer in bulk heterojuntion organic solar cells.

the gelation dynamics of the blends of P3Ht with small molecule acceptor under sub ambient conditions are highly sensitive to the shearing conditions, which in turn may lead to variations in the gel structure and hence the performance of the active layer in organic solar cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gelation behavior is a complex function of the shearing conditions, the polymer and the small molecule acceptor concentration and the solvent.
the gelation behavior and the gel strength of blends of P3 HT with small molecule acceptor o IDTB R are highly dependent on the shearing conditions during gelation.

rheology can be employed to characterize the gelation dynamics and gel structure of blends of P3 HT and small molecule acceptors and to understand how these blends may be processed to yield active layers for bulk heterojunction OSCs with enhanced performance.
